title: Nasal Dermatoses—Canine

content_blocks.text: Pathologic condition of the nasal skin involving either the haired portion (bridge of the nose/dorsal muzzle) or non-haired portion (nasal planum).

SLE—may see hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, evidence of glomerulonephritis (high BUN, proteinuria), joint disease, or other symptoms based on body system(s) affected.
Cytology— fungal organisms, bacteria, eosinophils (eosinophilic folliculitis and furunculosis), or acantholytic keratinocytes (pemphigus).

Antinuclear antibody (ANA)—positive in cases of SLE.
Electromyography (EMG)—evidence of polymyositis in SLE and dermatomyositis.
Direct immunofluorescence—deposition of immunoglobulin at the basement membrane zone in DLE, SLE, and PE, and intercellular spaces of epidermis in PF, PE, and PV.
